newsitem.title: UK: Northern dips as CE snaps up shares.
newsitem.headline: Northern dips as CE snaps up shares.

text.p: Shares in UK utility Northern Electric, the target of a hostile bid from the CE Electric unit of CalEnenergy Co, dipped on heavy volume on Friday even as CE's broker continued to snap up the shares, dealers said.
By 0926 GMT, Northern Electric shares were off 11p to 612-1/2p on trading volume of 2.8 million, placing them on London's most active list
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett, CE's broker, was said to be still buying the shares at the 630p bid price, and dealers reckon the predator's stake is now about 28 percent.
In a statement released yesterday, CE said it bought 6.5 million shares in the UK utility, boosting its stake in the firm to 19.9 percent.

"CE has picked up almost 30 percent now, so there's not going to be another bidder or an increased bid, and people are worried (the takeover) might be referred, so there's no upside anymore," said one.
